brief.greeting: Good morning. LLMs are finally learning to count their own words before you do.

stories.headline: TokenCast predicts LLM token use on the fly
stories.body: **Predictive token budgeting:** TokenCast learns a composable cost model so you can forecast how many tokens an LLM agent will spend as it runs, updating without extra model calls.
stories.why: Helps you avoid surprise API bills and plan prompt length.

stories.headline: KV‑streams speed up context compaction
stories.body: **Plug‑and‑play cache streaming:** KV‑streams accelerate agentic reinforcement‑learning training by 2.6–5×, shrinking context‑compaction time while keeping performance intact.
stories.why: Faster iteration on RL agents saves compute budget.

stories.headline: ESP32‑S3 renders detailed 3D with Jet Megatextures
stories.body: **Mipmapping on a microcontroller:** A Jet Megatextures demo shows the ESP32‑S3 can add texture detail to 3D scenes via mipmapping without overloading its modest GPU.
stories.why: Shows high‑fidelity graphics are possible on cheap IoT chips.

quick_hits.text: **Retro gaming:** Metal Gear Solid runs on an ESP32, proving classic code fits tiny silicon.
**Patch day:** Security updates hit AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Oracle—dozens of packages refreshed.
**Bottleneck hunting:** Argus uses an LLM to pinpoint OS‑level performance stalls without heavy tracing.
**Red‑team AI:** redamon automates offensive security workflows from start to finish.
**Tiny LLM playground:** MicroLLM Lab lets you run seven miniature models directly in the browser.

brief.sign_off: Catch you tomorrow, and keep those cycles humming (wink)

highlights.title: TokenCast: Forecasting Token Consumption During LLM Agent Execution
highlights.summary: TokenCast learns a composable cost representation for LLM agent execution segments, enabling token‑consumption forecasts that update as the run proceeds without extra LLM calls.
highlights.detail: The model records each segment's own token use and the context growth it adds, then composes adjacent segments to estimate cumulative cost, accounting for re‑reading earlier context in later calls. This approach tackles the order‑of‑magnitude variance seen across runs.

related.title: From PyTorch to the NPU: LLM-Agent-Driven Model Conversion Across Heterogeneous Inference Runtimes

highlights.title: KV-streams for Efficient Compaction in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
highlights.summary: KV‑streams provide a plug‑and‑play cache‑streaming method that boosts training throughput for agentic LLM context compaction by 2.6–5× without harming performance.
highlights.detail: By streaming the KV cache forward instead of flushing after each compaction, KV‑streams work with any existing compaction strategy and keep GPU memory usage constant. Experiments show consistent wall‑clock gains across three different compaction techniques.

related.title: MAGIC: Mixed-Granularity Agent Graphs via Incremental Construction with Dense-Reward Reinforcement Learning

highlights.title: Reasoning with Continuous Latent Diffusion
highlights.summary: Latent Flow Reasoning Models use continuous diffusion in latent space and a compact prompt encoder to replace a teacher Transformer at inference, improving reasoning efficiency.
highlights.detail: LFRMs train with an ELF‑based recipe, learning representations from multiple teacher layers and enabling asynchronous denoising at varied rates. A staged curriculum produces a prompt encoder that preserves only task‑relevant information, and self‑conditioning guidance further refines performance.

highlights.title: Jet Megatextures Demo for ESP32-S3
highlights.summary: A Jet Megatextures demo shows how mipmapping adds detail to 3D scenes on the ESP32‑S3 without overloading its rendering hardware.
highlights.detail: The technique stores multiple resolution levels of textures, allowing the ESP32‑S3 to display high‑quality graphics while conserving memory and processing power.

highlights.title: Metal Gear Solid Moves From PlayStation to ESP32
highlights.summary: A port of the original 1987 Metal Gear game runs on an ESP32 microcontroller, bringing the classic title to low‑cost hardware.
highlights.detail: The project demonstrates the ESP32's capability to emulate legacy game hardware, highlighting both the device's flexibility and the community's interest in retro gaming on embedded platforms.

items.title: Show HN: HN.watch – Videos of all Hacker News posts
items.summary: Scrimba Explain generates on‑the‑fly explainer videos for Hacker News links, costing about $0.04 per video and rendering in a few seconds.
items.detail: The system uses an HTML‑based video format rather than pixel‑level diffusion, which speeds creation and keeps editing cheap. Image generation, when used, can increase costs, but the core pipeline remains low‑cost and fast.

items.title: ESP32S3 cluster running 1.58-bit (BitNet) Language model
items.summary: An ESP32S3 cluster has been demonstrated running a 1.58‑bit BitNet language model.
items.detail: The setup showcases the feasibility of deploying quantized language models on low‑power microcontroller clusters, extending AI capabilities to edge devices with limited compute and memory resources.

items.title: MicroLLM Lab – Try 7 tiny LLM's in the browser
items.summary: MicroLLM Lab offers a browser‑based playground for trying seven tiny LLMs directly in the client.
items.detail: The platform runs the models entirely in WebAssembly/JavaScript, allowing users to experiment without server resources and demonstrating the practicality of ultra‑compact LLMs for interactive web applications.

items.title: How we will do better for Australia
items.summary: OpenAI apologised for incidents affecting Australian government websites and announced stronger safeguards and support to improve Australia's cyber defences.
items.detail: The statement acknowledges previous security lapses and outlines a plan to enhance protection mechanisms, including technical and operational measures, aimed at preventing future breaches.

items.title: Towards safety cases for frontier AI training
items.summary: OpenAI released early guidelines for safety cases in frontier AI training, covering technical safeguards, operational practices, and misalignment incident investigation.
items.detail: These guidelines aim to formalise risk assessment for advanced AI systems, providing a framework that developers can adopt to document safety measures and response procedures.

related.title: Building standards for the next phase of AI

items.title: Holo4: powering generalist computer-use agents
items.summary: Holo4 introduces a generalist computer‑use agent capable of performing a wide range of software tasks.
items.detail: The blog highlights the agent's ability to interpret visual cues and execute commands across different applications, positioning it as a step toward more versatile AI assistants.

items.title: Model: Viggle/Qwen-Image-2.1-viggle-turbo
items.summary: The Viggle/Qwen-Image-2.1‑viggle‑turbo model is a text‑to‑image generator with 175,907 downloads and 397 likes on Hugging Face.
items.detail: The model is listed among trending HF repos, indicating strong community interest; its popularity suggests it is competitive for generating images from textual prompts.

items.title: Jet Megatextures Demo for ESP32-S3
items.summary: A Jet Megatextures demo shows how mipmapping adds detail to 3D scenes on the ESP32‑S3 without overloading its rendering hardware.
items.detail: The technique stores multiple resolution levels of textures, allowing the ESP32‑S3 to display high‑quality graphics while conserving memory and processing power.

items.title: Metal Gear Solid Moves From PlayStation to ESP32
items.summary: A port of the original 1987 Metal Gear game runs on an ESP32 microcontroller, bringing the classic title to low‑cost hardware.
items.detail: The project demonstrates the ESP32's capability to emulate legacy game hardware, highlighting both the device's flexibility and the community's interest in retro gaming on embedded platforms.

items.title: Security updates for Monday
items.summary: Monday security updates were released for AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, and Oracle, covering dozens of packages such as Firefox, kernel, Chromium, PostgreSQL, and libxml2.
items.detail: The updates address vulnerabilities across a wide range of software stacks, from browsers and desktop environments to database extensions and system libraries. Each distribution lists its own set of affected packages, reflecting the heterogeneous nature of Linux ecosystems.

items.title: Show HN: PaperMono, e-ink fridge magnet shopping list with mobile web page
items.summary: PaperMono is an M5Stack ESP32‑S3 e‑ink fridge‑magnet that runs a 2,400‑line C++ firmware and syncs a shopping list via Wi‑Fi to a phone web app.
items.detail: The device uses the M5Stack PaperMono board with an e‑ink touchscreen and operates offline, storing the list locally until synchronization. The firmware was generated with Claude Code, demonstrating AI‑assisted development for embedded hardware.

items.title: [$] Reducing undefined behavior in the C language
items.summary: Martin Uecker presented at Kernel Recipes on reducing undefined behavior in C to move toward memory safety.
items.detail: Uecker, a biomedical engineering professor and long‑time Linux user, discussed challenges of undefined behavior in C and potential language or tooling changes that could improve safety for scientific and embedded applications.

items.title: Git v2.56.0 released
items.summary: Git 2.56.0 was released with 748 non‑merge commits contributed by 104 developers, including 39 first‑time contributors.
items.detail: The release adds a safer conflict‑resolution workflow, smaller path‑walk repacks, and a new "git history drop" sub‑command among other improvements. Development spanned several months since the June 2.55 release.

items.title: Argus: Agentic, Reference-Calibrated, Tree-Guided, System-Software-Level Bottleneck Localization
items.summary: Argus is an LLM‑driven system that localizes OS‑level bottlenecks by analyzing code paths without heavy instrumentation.
items.detail: Targeting the growing CPU orchestration role in heterogeneous workloads, Argus combines agentic reasoning with reference‑calibrated models to pinpoint slowdown sources across subsystems like memory management and networking, reducing the need for repeated kernel tracing.

items.title: Session Type State Spaces Form Lattices
items.summary: Session type state spaces form bounded lattices; evaluation on 108 protocols showed 93 distributive and 15 non‑distributive lattices.
items.detail: The work proves lattice properties for well‑formed session types and demonstrates duality and subtyping correspondences. Implementations were mechanised in Lean 4 with two independent tools, confirming the theoretical results across diverse benchmarks.

items.title: Monitoring and Verification of Multitenant Kubernetes Clusters using TLA+ Trace Checking
items.summary: A monitoring tool uses TLA+ trace checking on Kubernetes audit logs to detect multitenancy violations in live clusters.
items.detail: The approach repurposes TLA+ specifications from design‑time model checking to runtime verification, allowing formal reasoning to be applied continuously. While focused on multitenancy, the pipeline can be adapted to other policy checks in Kubernetes environments.

items.title: On Asynchrony and Reversibility in CCS
items.summary: The paper introduces CCSa, an asynchronous variant of CCS that integrates reversible computation with explicit message entities.
items.detail: CCSa separates output actions from consumption, enabling messages to be treated as first‑class objects that can be undone while preserving causal dependencies. This extends reversible semantics, previously limited to synchronous CCS, to more realistic asynchronous settings.

items.title: Semantic Prefix Oracles for LLM Decoding: Contracts and Differential Validation
items.summary: Semantic Prefix Oracles enforce context‑sensitive constraints during LLM decoding, rejecting only irreparable prefixes.
items.detail: The system augments a context‑free grammar with semantic checks (e.g., scope, typing) executed during Earley parsing, guaranteeing dead‑end freedom for remaining branches. It succeeds on finite‑lambda, core ML, and C‑like fragments, but not on plain STLC, which can produce unrepairable type errors.

items.title: Torch-PIM: Automated Profile-Guided PIM Offloading for PyTorch
items.summary: Torch-PIM adds profile‑guided placement of PyTorch loops onto processing‑in‑memory units to reduce data‑movement bottlenecks.
items.detail: The compiler framework profiles each parallel loop nest for work amount and memory boundedness, then decides host versus PIM execution. Unlike prior offloading tools that target hand‑written code or fixed operator lists, Torch‑PIM works on the progressive lowering stages of PyTorch programs.

items.title: samugit83/redamon
items.summary: samugit83/redamon is an AI‑driven red‑team framework that automates the full offensive security workflow without human input.
items.detail: The tool chains reconnaissance, exploitation, and post‑exploitation steps, leveraging language models to generate and execute actions. It is positioned as a fully autonomous penetration‑testing platform for continuous security assessment.

items.title: Detanup01/gbe_fork
items.summary: Detanup01/gbe_fork is a C++ fork of the Goldberg emulator project hosted on GitLab.
items.detail: The repository mirrors the original Goldberg emulator codebase, allowing developers to experiment with or extend the emulator under a separate GitHub namespace.

items.title: PrismLauncher/PrismLauncher
items.summary: PrismLauncher is a custom Minecraft launcher that lets users manage multiple game installations simultaneously, built as a fork of MultiMC.
items.detail: The tool is written in C++ and targets both Windows and Linux platforms. It retains MultiMC's feature set while adding a modern UI and easier profile handling. Users can switch between different Minecraft versions, mod packs, and Java runtimes without reinstalling.

items.title: Rizzo-AI-Academy/rizzo-pii
items.summary: Rizzo-pii is a Python library that anonymizes documents locally before they are sent to large language models, protecting personal data.
items.detail: It operates entirely on the user's machine, removing or redacting PII such as names, addresses, and IDs. The library provides a simple API for integration into existing pipelines and supports common document formats like TXT and PDF. By avoiding network transmission of raw data, it reduces privacy risks when using external LLM services.

items.title: SerenityOS/serenity
items.summary: SerenityOS is an open-source operating system written in C++ that aims to recreate a classic desktop environment with modern development practices.
items.detail: The project includes its own kernel, GUI, and a suite of native applications, all built from scratch. It emphasizes code readability and educational value, often showcasing retro-inspired design while supporting contemporary hardware. Contributors regularly add features like a web browser, text editor, and file manager.

items.title: ThirteenAG/WidescreenFixesPack
items.summary: WidescreenFixesPack provides plugins that add or improve widescreen resolution support for various games, fixing related bugs and adding features.
items.detail: The collection targets titles that originally lacked proper aspect‑ratio handling, enabling smoother gameplay on modern monitors. Plugins are written in C++ and can be applied via simple installers or manual injection. Community contributions keep the pack updated with new games and fixes.
